title: fleet-priming-reflection-2027-02-18
body:
Weekly infrastructure log — GPU fleet, regions, capacity planning (notes + decisions)

Period covered: 2027-02-08 to 2027-02-14
Author: Aisha Patel (infra oncall)
Attendees (standup/working session): Marco Ruiz, Chen Li, Samira Gomez, Devon Clarke, oncall rotation and SRE rotation

Purpose: capture the outcomes of the week’s cross-functional syncs about fleet priming (prewarming), regional capacity posture, and the short-term capacity plan for the upcoming product rollout next month. This is an operational working note — action items are tracked below.

1) Quick summary / headline
- We validated the priming experiment across a mixed workload (chat + embedding rerank) for the 8k-context family. Cold-start p50 latency dropped ~60% with a 45-minute adaptive priming window.
- Net effect on available GPU-hours: priming increases baseline utilization by ~6% in west-us and eu-west under our test traffic; APAC shows more variability (spikes during business hours).
- Capacity headroom as of snapshot (2027-02-14 23:00 UTC): west-us +12% nominal, eu-west +8%, apac-southeast +3% (risky for peak).
- Decision: adopt a conservative priming schedule for west-us and eu-west for next three weeks; hold on broad priming in APAC until homogeneous traffic smoothing is in place.

2) Data and telemetry reviewed
- Metric highlights from the week:
  - Cold-start p50 (unprimed) for 8k models: 420ms median across regions; with priming: 170ms p50.
  - Token throughput per GPU (8k model): +4% after primed cache reuse during sustained bursts.
  - Idle-hours consumed by priming: roughly 0.25 GPU-hours per primed instance per day.
  - Error spike correlation: two small load-shedding events in APAC coincided with auto-scaler lag during a regional burst (2027-02-11 04:12 UTC).
- Dashboards referenced: per-route latency (console -> infra/routing -> model-8k), priming heatmap (daily), regional-utilization-week. Links in linked_artifacts.

3) Region-specific notes
- west-us (primary):
  - Observations: steady background traffic, predictable diurnal pattern. Prewarming succeeded with low cost impact thanks to spare capacity.
  - Plan: enable adaptive priming on model-8k and model-16k canary routes; priming windows 30–60 minutes depending on route SLI.

- eu-west (secondary):
  - Observations: slightly higher baseline utilization than west-us but still safe for conservative priming.
  - Plan: enable priming for non-enterprise routes first, measure 1-week impact, then expand.

- apac-southeast (edge):
  - Observations: shallow headroom, noisy burst patterns from partner integrations. Two mid-week preemption events increased queue latency by 220ms temporarily.
  - Plan: postpone priming; instead focus on local autoscaler tuning and request-routing improvements. Short-term measure: route heavy-burst customers to dedicated pools (see action item #3).

4) Capacity planning and short-term hedges
- Forecast: With product rollout (project Aurora) scheduled for 2027-03-10, expected ~18% increase in peak token/sec across public routes. If priming is applied indiscriminately, we estimate a 10–12% additional GPU-hour burn during priming windows.
- Hedging options evaluated:
  - Ramp dedicated pool reservations for west-us by +20 cards for March (cost estimate attached to ticket JIRA-OPS-1428).
  - Use burstable capacity from partner cloud region for APAC for 6 weeks starting 2027-03-01 (negotiation ongoing).
  - Selective throttling: increase per-account concurrency caps for high-SLA customers to avoid overloading edge pools.
- Decision made in meeting: short-term mix of (1) +20 west-us dedicated cards and (2) temporary routing of three heavy APAC customers to the Dedicated pool during peak windows. CTO approval for allocation pending finance sign-off.

5) Operational incidents and root-cause notes
- Incident: 2027-02-11 04:10 UTC — regional autoscaler stuck in startup path, caused 3-min priority queue spike
  - RCA notes: race condition between preemption handler and scale-down suppression flag. Patch in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/876. Needs additional unit tests for the suppression flow.
- Incident: sporadic higher preemption rate in APAC due to cloud provider reclaim -> matched to partner maintenance windows. We will add provider-maintenance signals to our capacity-scouting pipeline.

6) Experiments & follow-ups from the week
- Priming tuning experiment (A/B):
  - Variant A: aggressive priming (60m warm window) vs Variant B: adaptive (traffic-triggered 15–45m).
  - Result: Variant B preserved headroom while delivering 90% of latency improvement. Recommend adaptive as default.
- Autoscaler tuning: added a jittered reconciliation loop and raised the cooldown to 45s. Preliminary reduction in flapping observed (from 9 events/day to 2 events/day in the canary cohort).
- KV-cache TTL experiments: small gains when TTL set to 2h for conversational routes; further eval required for cost tradeoffs.

7) Action items (owner — due)
- Aisha: finalize priming playbook edits with adaptive schedule and rollout checklist — due 2027-02-19.
- Marco: open PR for unit tests around scale-down suppression (followup on PR#876) — due 2027-02-20.
- Chen: negotiate 6-week APAC burst agreement with cloud partner and share preliminary cost estimate — due 2027-02-22.
- Samira: implement routing override for three APAC customers to Dedicated pool (proof-of-concept) — due 2027-02-24.
- Devon: add provider-maintenance signals to capacity-scouting pipeline and add a health check to preemption alerting — due 2027-02-21.

8) Open questions and risks
- How sustainable is priming long-term as model families change? We need a cross-team rubric for priming thresholds (token cost vs latency SLO improvement).
- If APAC partner agreement falls through, we will have <1% headroom during weekday peaks — contingency is to throttle non-critical routes and escalate capacity purchases.
- Finance approval is needed for the west-us card ramp; if denied, fallback is to delay priming expansion and rely on more aggressive caching on client side.

9) Notes to future oncall / handover
- If you pick up oncall: review the priming heatmap, and if APAC queue latency exceeds 300ms for >3 consecutive 5-min windows, flip the routing override for the designated APAC customers (Samira’s runbook).
- Tag slack channel #infra-ops and escalate to paging list if routing overrides are insufficient.

Appendix (short logs)
- 2027-02-09 10:03 UTC — Canary priming enabled in west-us for model-8k (canary cohort = 5% production traffic).
- 2027-02-11 04:10 UTC — Autoscaler incident (see RCA).
- 2027-02-12 15:20 UTC — Adaptive priming variant B measurement snapshot taken (attached in monitoring).

End of note. Please leave comments inline or ping in #infra-ops for urgent edits.
